fabdfd1e7e: Overview: LineXinBar, the XMB-style console desktop for Linux
38bc9538e2: LineXinBar pairs a lightweight Wayland compositor with a controller-friendly XMB launcher: browse your games, apps and media, and switch between screens, with a gamepad, a keyboard or a mouse.
6a0e787505: For your games, apps and media
dcc8af2461: LineXinBar is a console-style Linux desktop for your games, apps and media. It pairs a lightweight Wayland compositor with a launcher you drive with a gamepad, a keyboard or a mouse.
fba8157da6: Browse your library, open ordinary desktop applications and switch between screens from one interface in the manner of the PlayStation 3's XrossMediaBar (XMB) — a bar of categories across the screen, a column of what is in each one, and a guide one button away over anything that is running. It is the whole session, not an app on top of another desktop: the file manager, the settings, the password prompts and the update screen are all part of it, all reachable from the sofa.
24b11b2d32: LineXinBar's start screen: a row of category tiles with Games lit, and the Games column below it with Steam and RetroArch, on a purple wallpaper with a flowing band of light
733390ff11: The start screen, on the Games column.
1f4c96df0d: Apps, music, videos and pictures with a controller, and an on-screen keyboard when you need to type.
c528fbe0bd: Steam, and optionally Epic Games, your own console games through RetroArch, and PlayStation 3 through RPCS3.
218fad9d4f: Each screen at its own resolution and refresh rate, with its own bar.
0c3af08571: Switch apps, change the volume and brightness, or get back to the launcher — from inside anything.
f81331a50f: Twelve accents, a wallpaper of water or silk or your own film, ten languages.
9ed2a18aa2: Files, screenshots, screen sharing, file dialogs and system updates, alongside your apps.
fa79fe2085: Captured from a nested session of the project's own release build.
19a059b63c: The Settings column with Updates lit, followed by Appearance, Language and Display
7593f0615e: Settings, the shell's own column, with Updates at its head.
4e1b1e15c4: The guide open over the start screen, with the time, quick settings, a volume bar and Resume
60b7d05b38: The guide, over whatever is running.
f6484dc9e6: The login screen on two displays side by side
be13420e3a: The login screen made to go with it, on two displays.
e5e8745b9c: Gamescope owns one output and scales one application onto it. LineXinBar keeps the same small "one application fills the screen" model — but every connected display is a real output with its own render loop.
9ed6027d02: Displays with different resolutions and refresh rates therefore run independently, rather than being locked to a shared heartbeat, and each has a start screen of its own. It is a whole desktop session rather than a game's frame: applications, files, settings and prompts all live in it.
bcb5ff1908: LineXinBar is in early development, at version 0.9.3.
3e8ab4f4eb: Hardware testing has mainly covered one AMD graphics card with two displays; other vendors and multi-GPU setups need more people trying them.
856e5b2661: Steam games need Valve's Steam client, which runs out of sight. Epic Games, RetroArch and PlayStation 3 are optional packages.
25147c4f44: Sharing a single window (rather than a whole display), gesture navigation and variable refresh rate are not there yet.
d07d0e3d21: Read the known limitations before relying on it as your everyday desktop — and if you try it on your hardware, say how it went.
